data.title: Sanofi Targets Teen Acne With New mRNA Vaccine Trial, Opening a Fresh Growth Avenue for SNY
data.description:
Sanofi SA (SNY) announced an update on their ongoing clinical study.

Sanofi SA (SNY) is launching a Phase 1/2 trial called “A Phase 1/2, Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-controlled Study to Evaluate the Safety of an Acne mRNA Vaccine Candidate in Adolescents 12 to 17 Years of Age With Moderate to Severe Acne.” The study aims to test safety at several dose levels in teens, a group with high unmet need and strong potential demand for new acne solutions.

The treatment is an intramuscular acne mRNA vaccine, given as a series of three injections at different dose levels, compared with placebo shots. The goal is to prevent or reduce moderate to severe acne in 12–17 year olds by training the body to better manage acne-related triggers over time.

The trial is interventional and randomized, with participants split by chance into vaccine or placebo groups across several subcohorts and main cohorts. It uses a triple-blind setup, meaning participants, site doctors, and outcome assessors do not know who gets the vaccine, and its main focus is on prevention rather than treatment of existing lesions alone.

The study was first submitted on Aug. 4, 2026, and is listed as not yet recruiting, signaling that site activation and enrollment are still ahead. The most recent update was filed on Sept. 15, 2026, showing that Sanofi is actively refining the protocol; primary and final completion dates have not yet been posted and will guide later data readouts and market expectations.

For investors, this study marks Sanofi’s push to extend mRNA beyond infectious disease into a large, chronic dermatology market. If early safety data are favorable, sentiment toward SNY could benefit as the firm diversifies against rivals like Moderna and other dermatology players, though revenue impact remains long-term and will hinge on future efficacy results and regulatory progress.

The study remains active in setup and recently updated, with more details and ongoing changes available on the ClinicalTrials portal.

data.title: Gold.com appoints new CFO and changes auditor
data.description:
Gold.com ( (GOLD) ) just unveiled an announcement.

On September 18, 2026, Gold.com announced that Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer Cary Dickson retired, having submitted his resignation on September 14, 2026, and will remain with the company as a consultant for 12 months. Effective the same day, Executive Vice President, Controller and Assistant Secretary Jill Van was appointed CFO and principal financial and accounting officer under a new employment agreement running through June 30, 2029, with a $500,000 base salary, performance-based bonus opportunity and time-vested restricted stock units.

Van, who joined Gold.com in June 2025 and brings more than 25 years of accounting and financial leadership experience at public accounting firms and private companies, steps into the role after previously serving as interim CFO and audit partner at several firms. Also effective in mid-September 2026, the audit committee appointed KPMG LLP as Gold.com’s independent registered public accounting firm for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2027, replacing Grant Thornton LLP as the company aligns its finance leadership and auditor relationships with its expanding global operations.
